newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Dow recovery helps shares, markets await Fed.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Dow recovery helps shares, markets await Fed.

text.p: European bourses generally recovered their composure on Tuesday after a sharp overnight rebound on Wall Street, which surfaced from an early 50 point dive to close slightly up.
London, Frankfurt and Paris, which all closed well down on Monday and London suffering its biggest drop in two months, opened higher on Tuesday, although London fell back later.
The Dow ended up 6.28 points at a record 5,894.74.
But stock and currency markets were effectively holding their breath ahead of a crucial U.S. monetary policy-making meeting later in the day.

Dealers and analysts were deeply divided over whether the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) committee would sanction a credit tightening after the meeting (at 1300 GMT), the outcome of which would not be known until after European markets closed. If the Fed decided to increase interest rates, it would be the first rise for 1-1/2 years.
British stocks lost their opening gains and were trading near the day's lows by late morning as banks succumbed to a wave of institutional profit-taking and other stocks were mixed, traders said.
The blue chip FTSE 100 was down 9.6 points at 3910.1 by 1100 GMT. Bank stocks HSBC, Barclays and NatWest led the retreat and decliners were in a three-to-one majority.

A money-market signal from the Bank of England that it had, as expected, left interest rates unchanged after the government's monthly monetary meeting made little impact on shares. Nor did reports showing a stronger-than-expected 2.2 percent British GDP growth in the second quarter.
"The market felt pretty good this morning but right now it feels horrible," said the head of equity trading at one top brokerage as the FTSE 100 plumbed the day's depths.
Another trader said: "I would think the market would take a quarter-point hike in its stride but at the moment we just don't want to do anything."

In Frankfurt, German shares held on to small morning gains ahead of the Fed meeting but volumes were generally limited and trading range seen very tight. Dollar strength continued to lend some support to stocks, dealers said, and government bonds were also slightly higher.

On the Paris bourse stocks moved up from a higher opening buoyed by Wall Street. Metals, however, were hit by disappointing results from steelmaker Usinor, down two francs after reporting a 65 percent drop in first half profits. On the currency front, too, the mood was one of wait and see. The dollar was stuck in a tiny range by midday in Europe and dealers said all eyes were on the Fed amid confusion over what impact its decision would have on the market.
A quarter-point rise in the federal funds target rate was largely discounted, but analysts were deeply divided over whether the FOMC would sanction a change in U.S. monetary policy at all.
CURRENCIES AT 1100 GMT
The dollar was at 1.5125 marks and 109.78 yen compared with 1.5120 marks and 109.88 yen in Europe late on Monday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1100
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was 9.6 points down at 3,910.1.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was 12.95 points up at 2,080.04.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt was up 11.19 at 2,638.23.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed firmer at $381.60 compared with Monday's London Gold close of $381.25. Silver was also firmer at $4.90 cents.
